crime: Every evening at half past eight, the same girl found the jug on the library table already full: {WITCH_NAME} had melted into it. The girl carried it to the upper railing and poured it into the courtyard fountain, loving to watch {WITCH_NAME} fall, shining. Once the courtyard emptied, {WITCH_NAME} rose from the fountain.
Long ago, {WITCH_NAME}'s father had held her floating in a river. "I've got you," he said. She looked up and saw him on the bank, lacing his shoes. That week he was gone.
One night in the courtyard, the girl put the empty jug into {WITCH_NAME}'s hands. "Tomorrow, pour yourself wherever you like." The hands that held her had let go.

The next evening at half past eight, the girl poured the full jug from the railing into the fountain while the prisoners below watched, as always. Then she sat reading in the library by the unwilting cherry tree, and {WITCH_NAME} strangled her from behind with both hands.

The prisoners sat round the basin from the pour until the shout; no girl rose from the water. At half past nine, a prisoner found the body in the library, the jug on the table beside it, and shouted. {WITCH_NAME} appeared in the second-floor hall behind the running crowd, saying she had risen at the shout.

In the trial court, the prisoners concluded that {WITCH_NAME} had lain in the fountain as water while someone else went upstairs. Then a prisoner tilted the jug: water still sat in the bottom. When {WITCH_NAME} reformed, she gathered back every drop; once she rose, the jug was always dry. The prisoner understood. Plain water had been poured, and {WITCH_NAME} had never left the second floor.
fields.epitaph: Asked only where she would run, she chose the one way that stopped the hands.
fields.epithet: Water that waits to be poured
execution: The execution stand raised a tall glass tank of river water. She floated face up inside it on two iron palms, her ankles shackled. One palm slid out from under her, then the other. The water closed over her face, and the shackles drew her down to the floor of the tank. She lay still at the bottom, the two iron palms open and empty above her.

magic.name: Meltwater
magic.text: She can melt into running water and gather herself back again.
